20261119-physics-g11.s.s1.prompt: Object A of mass 3 kg and object B of mass 2 kg are placed in contact on a frictionless horizontal surface, and a horizontal force of 20 N is applied to push on the A side. What are the acceleration of the two objects and the magnitude of the force with which A pushes B, respectively?
20261119-physics-g11.s.s1.explain: The overall acceleration is $a = \frac{F}{m_A + m_B} = \frac{20\text{ N}}{5\text{ kg}} = 4\text{ m/s}^2$. The only net force accelerating object B is the contact force with which A pushes B, so $F_{AB} = m_B \cdot a = 2\text{ kg} \times 4\text{ m/s}^2 = 8\text{ N}$.
20261119-physics-g11.s.s1.hint.0: For the whole system (A + B): F = (m_A + m_B) a → 20 = (3 + 2) a
20261119-physics-g11.s.s1.hint.1: Net force on B = force A exerts on B = m_B × a

20261121-physics-g11-2.s.s1.hint.0: When a wave crest meets a trough, 'destructive interference' occurs and the amplitude becomes 0.

20261119-physics-g12.thinking.0: A charged particle of mass m and charge q
20261119-physics-g12.s.s1.prompt: A charged particle of mass m and charge q enters perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B at speed v and undergoes uniform circular motion. Which option correctly gives the radius r and period T of its circular orbit?
20261119-physics-g12.s.s1.explain: From the centripetal force equation, $\frac{mv^2}{r} = qvB \implies r = \frac{mv}{qB}$. The period is $T = \frac{2\pi r}{v} = \frac{2\pi m}{qB}$, and, remarkably, this cyclotron period is independent of the orbit radius and speed.
20261119-physics-g12.s.s1.hint.0: The Lorentz force acts as the centripetal force of the circular motion: q v B = m v² / r

20261122-physics-g12-1.material: [Advanced 2D mechanics] The maximum horizontal range R of a projectile launched from the ground at angle θ above the horizontal with initial speed v₀ is R = (v₀² sin 2θ) / g. With no air resistance, what launch angle θ gives the maximum horizontal range, and what other launch angle gives the same horizontal range as a launch angle of 30°?
20261122-physics-g12-1.s.s1.prompt: [Advanced 2D mechanics] The maximum horizontal range R of a projectile launched from the ground at angle θ above the horizontal with initial speed v₀ is R = (v₀² sin 2θ) / g. With no air resistance, what launch angle θ gives the maximum horizontal range, and what other launch angle gives the same horizontal range as a launch angle of 30°?
20261122-physics-g12-1.s.s1.explain: The condition for $\sin 2\theta$ to be maximum is $2\theta = 90^\circ \implies \theta = 45^\circ$. Also, since $\sin(2 \times 30^\circ) = \sin 60^\circ = \sin 120^\circ = \sin(2 \times 60^\circ)$, the range is the same at the angle ($60^\circ$) that makes the sum of the angles $90^\circ$.

20261122-physics-g12-2.title: intense beam without spreading far
20261122-physics-g12-2.goal: Sebenzisa izimiso ze-intense beam without spreading far ukuxazulula inkinga yophenyo.
20261122-physics-g12-2.material: What is the decisive wave property that lets a laser beam travel as a thin, intense beam without spreading far, unlike an incandescent lamp or sunlight?
20261122-physics-g12-2.s.s1.prompt: What is the decisive wave property that lets a laser beam travel as a thin, intense beam without spreading far, unlike an incandescent lamp or sunlight?
20261122-physics-g12-2.s.s1.explain: Laser light is produced by stimulated emission. It is monochromatic, with the wavelengths of all emitted photons extremely closely matched, and its wave phases match perfectly (coherent), giving it outstanding directionality and focusability.
20261122-physics-g12-2.s.s1.hint.0: It is light amplified by stimulated emission.
20261122-physics-g12-2.s.s1.hint.1: Its phase and frequency are perfectly aligned.
20261122-physics-g12-2.s.s1.o.o0: Excellent coherence and monochromaticity, in which the wavelength and phase of all photons match perfectly
20261122-physics-g12-2.s.s1.o.o1: Because the speed of light is 10 times faster than that of ordinary light
20261122-physics-g12-2.s.s1.o.o2: Because a laser is a beam of charged particles
20261122-physics-g12-2.s.s1.o.o3: Because it can travel only in a vacuum
